materials.notes: Assessed at both stages; headline SR is the extraction-stage value (higher of the two). Annex 2 stage SRs: extraction 1.2, processing 0.5. Import reliance is for the extraction stage; processing-stage import reliance is 58% (Annex 10). Table 6 of the study prints Guinea 63% as main EU supplier. All figures are for bauxite (extraction stage); the study merged aluminium and bauxite into one entry in 2023. Processing-stage (primary aluminium) figures from Annex 7/8: global producers China 55.6%, Russia 6.0%, India 5.5%; EU sourcing Russia 19%, Germany 10%, Mozambique 9%. Table 15 of the study prints SR 1.1 / EI 5.5 for 'Aluminium' in 2023, which differs from Annex 2 (SR 1.2 / EI 5.8 for aluminium/bauxite); the Annex 2 results table is used.

materials.notes: Group value for the ten heavy rare earth elements (Dy, Er, Eu, Gd, Ho, Lu, Tb, Tm, Yb, Y); the study also scores each element separately (SR 3.3-5.6, EI 2.9-7.8). Assessed at both stages; headline SR is the processing-stage value (higher of the two). Annex 2 stage SRs: extraction 2.3, processing 5.1. EoL-RIR is null because the study gives two different values: 1% in Annex 11 (the table of rates used in the assessment, also plotted in Figure 8) and 4% in the Annex 1 overview table. Global producer share is the processing-stage group figure (China 100% for every HREE in Annex 7). EU sourcing left empty: Annex 1 gives n/a and the report says HREEs are excluded from the EU sourcing analysis for lack of reliable data, although Table 6 prints China 100%. Strategic status applies to the 'rare earth elements for permanent magnets' entry of Annex I, which covers the HREEs Tb, Dy and Gd only.

caveats: All values were parsed from the PDF of the 2023 Final Report (tables extracted programmatically) and cross-checked between the report's own tables. Nothing was filled from memory.

The report is internally inconsistent in places. Every disagreement that affects this dataset is listed under 'conflicts' with the candidate values and their table/page. Where the disagreement could not be settled the field is null (or the list is empty).

eol_rir_pct is null for 7 materials (heavy-rare-earths, light-rare-earths, phosphate-rock, platinum-group-metals, tantalum, titanium-metal, vanadium) because Annex 11 and the Annex 1 overview give different rates.

supply_risk is the value at the stage with the higher supply risk (the study's rule); assessed_stage says which. import_reliance_pct, global_producers and eu_sourcing refer to that same stage unless an entry's own 'stage' says otherwise.

global_producers shares are from Annex 7 (one decimal) and eu_sourcing shares from Annex 8 (whole percent, sources of 1% or more, EU domestic production plus imports). The report's Annex 1 and Tables 5/6 show the same data rounded, sometimes differing by one point.
Heavy rare earths, light rare earths and platinum group metals carry group values; per-element results exist in the study but are not in this file.

Data reflect 2016-2020 supply patterns. They predate later shifts (for example in gallium, germanium, nickel and lithium markets) and should be labelled as the 2023 assessment, not as current market shares.

is_strategic follows Annex I Section 1 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1252 as published in the Official Journal on 3 May 2024 (17 entries); several entries are grade-specific (battery grade, metallurgy grade, magnesium metal, rare earths for permanent magnets) - see notes.
Copper and nickel do not meet the criticality thresholds; they are on the list of 34 because strategic raw materials are automatically critical.
Page numbers in source_refs and conflicts are the report's printed page numbers (PDF page = printed page + 4).
RMIS raw material profiles were consulted only to help judge conflicts; they mix 2023-assessment figures with newer data and are not the source of any value here.
